svg.title: The MRTR loop drawn as five messages across three lifelines
svg.desc: A sequence diagram with three lifelines: the user, the host and its client, and the server. Five numbered steps run down the page. One, the client sends a tools/call carrying a name, arguments and _meta. Two, the server answers with a result whose resultType is input_required, carrying inputRequests and a requestState, and a tag beside the server reads then forgets everything. Three, marked off the wire, the host renders the question to the user on a dashed arrow and the user answers accept, decline or cancel on a dashed arrow back; no MCP message is involved. Four, the client sends a second tools/call with the same arguments and _meta plus inputResponses and the same requestState. Five, the server returns a result whose resultType is complete. A note along the bottom says step four carries a new JSON-RPC id, is a new request rather than a continuation, and may be answered by a different replica than step one, so everything the server needs is in that message or it is gone.
svg.text: The server does not ask. It answers, and waits to be asked again.
Two complete JSON-RPC exchanges. Nothing stays open between them, so nothing has to be remembered.
Step 4 carries a new JSON-RPC id. It is a new request, not a continuation, and it may be answered by a
different replica than step 1. Everything the server needs is in that message, or it is gone.
